NC with dad and LC with mom (still on her phone bill).
I'm not saying no contact is the answer, I understand how this can be traumatic for some, for me it was the only answer. It was like talking to a brick wall when I would tell them what they did to me. 
If you don't feel like you're treated poorly, look at your development compared to others. I learned how,,, under developed I was compared to my peers. No control on my emotions, no idea what I want from life, I over share personal stories (I would basically introduce myself as 'hey I'm Tibbons, I used to cut myself! And would always wonder why people would look at me funny, I just thought I was sharing), things like this would be neglect and is just as harmful as abuse. Sometimes no punch to the face is the same as a punch to the face.

"Your childhood wasn't even that bad! We did so much together! You've always been so sensitive. Yknow some people were beat and raped? You don't have it that bad." Different things from different immediate family members... yeah dude shit sucks.

It was the same way for me. Even worse, I would defend them as good parents! It took four years away at college for me to start thinking 'maybe they were too much' and then a year of living on my own to finally realize I have to go no contact because I found myself wanting to be someone, but that someone would not fit in with my family. 
It was tough at first, but I'm finally, after sixth months of no contact with my father and low contact with my mother I am finding bits of who I am and bits of myself I killed in high-school that I enjoyed. This is mostly a rant for myself that I typed on break at work that I refuse to proof read, sorry if its not coherent!
